fact: Neither Rinn Valley Ranch's Design Guidelines nor its Declaration mentions artificial turf, synthetic turf or putting greens (searched September 26, 2026).
quote: Full-text search of the Design Guidelines (Revision 7.2) and the Declaration of Covenants, Conditions and Restrictions for "artificial", "synthetic", "putting" and "turf": no provision on artificial turf or putting greens; the only "turf" is the drainage-ditch rule, "Native vegetation, turf, or cobbles are the only acceptable landscaping alternatives for the drainage ditches."
source_label: Rinn Valley Ranch Design Guidelines, Revision 7.2 (updated 12/10/2024), full text, and the Declaration of Covenants, Conditions and Restrictions of Rinn Valley Ranch (recorded November 13, 2002)
notes: Both documents are linked from https://www.rinnvalleyranch.org/hoa-documents (Design Guidelines; Covenants; Covenants First Amendment, acknowledged July 14, 2003). The Declaration was read as the Google Doc export of https://docs.google.com/document/d/151V0Py7W-POef_BXk-e1OiU8oImMuyCF/edit; the First Amendment was searched too and has none of these words. "Artificial" does not occur in the guidelines; "synthetic" occurs only in the exterior-materials clause (Sec. 3.5: synthetic stone, brick and stucco).

fact: Rinn Valley Ranch's Design Guidelines require complete landscaping plans for any change to a front or back yard, and no landscaping may start until the Design Committee approves them.
quote: The Design Committee requires complete landscaping plans for any changes for landscaping to front or back yards. No landscaping shall commence until plans are approved by the Design Committee.
source_label: Rinn Valley Ranch Design Guidelines, Revision 7.2 (updated 12/10/2024), Sec. 3.19.1 Landscaping

fact: Rinn Valley Ranch's Declaration counts grading, drainage changes, sprinkler systems, patios, sod, gravel and other landscaping as Improvements, and none may be built or altered without the committee's written approval.
quote: (b) The grading, excavation, filling or similar disturbance to the surface of the land including, without limitation, change of grade, change of ground level, change of drainage pattern; (c) All landscaping features, including, but not limited to, building, outbuilding, swimming pools, tennis courts, patios, patio covers, awnings, … walkways, sprinkle systems, … fences, screening walls, retaining walls, stairs, decks, landscaping, hedges, windbreaks, plantings, trees, shrubs, flowers, vegetables, sod, gravel, bark, exterior light fixtures … No Improvement of any kind shall be erected, altered, placed, modified, or maintained within The Planned Community unless and until the final plans, elevations, and specifications thereof have received written approval by the Committee as herein provided.
source_label: Declaration of Covenants, Conditions and Restrictions of Rinn Valley Ranch, Sec. 1.25(b)-(c) and Sec. 6.4

fact: Rinn Valley Ranch exempts only a short list of changes from design review, such as planting to an approved plan or adding plants that mature under 24 inches, and sends every other landscaping or site change to the committee.
quote: The additional of permanent planting materials that do not conform to an approved landscape plan as long as the mature size of the planting does not exceed 24 inches in height including flowers and vegetable gardens. … Only those items listed above are exempt from the Design Committee process. All other types of residential construction, development, landscaping, site modification, and other such items must be submitted to the Design Review Committee.
source_label: Rinn Valley Ranch Design Guidelines, Revision 7.2 (updated 12/10/2024), Sec. 4.1.3 Exceptions

fact: Rinn Valley Ranch's guidelines require live vegetative cover on 70% of the front yard, not counting the house, driveway and drainage ditch, count gravel or mulch only where plants are installed, and limit it to brown, gray or Colorado sandstone colors.
quote: Seventy percent (70%) of the front yard exclusive of the portion occupied by the house, driveway and drainage ditch, shall be covered with live vegetative cover. Gravel and mulch shall not be considered live vegetative cover unless plants, shrubs and trees have been installed. Areas of gravel or mulch shall be of brown, gray or Colorado sandstone color ranges. … Please refer to the Colorado Waterwise guidelines for Xeriscape
source_label: Rinn Valley Ranch Design Guidelines, Revision 7.2 (updated 12/10/2024), Sec. 3.19.6 and 3.19.7
notes: Arithmetic, not a quote: the front yard's remaining 30% may be non-live cover. The guidelines do not say how artificial turf counts; read plainly it is not live vegetative cover.

fact: Rinn Valley Ranch owners must keep the drainage ditch along the street in native vegetation, turf or 4- to 6-inch cobble and keep it clear so water flows freely.
quote: All Lot Owners are required to maintain the native vegetation, replace with turf or use 4- to 6- inch cobble as depicted on the Drainage Ditch Detail attached hereto as Exhibit C. In either case, the Lot Owners are responsible for maintenance of the drainage ditches and keeping them free of obstructions and overgrowth so the water can flow freely. Native vegetation, turf, or cobbles are the only acceptable landscaping alternatives for the drainage ditches.
source_label: Rinn Valley Ranch Design Guidelines, Revision 7.2 (updated 12/10/2024), Sec. 3.19.4
notes: The guidelines do not say whether "turf" here includes artificial turf; the Declaration (Sec. 7.23) also makes each owner landscape and maintain the ditch abutting the lot.

fact: Rinn Valley Ranch's committee responds within 30 days, a landscaping-only request needs just plans and the fee, and a complete request not disapproved within 30 days is deemed approved.
quote: The Design Committee will respond within thirty (30) days after submittal, provided that the plans are in accordance with the requirements outlined below. If only landscaping is involved, only plans and the fee are required. … Unless disapproval is transmitted to the applicant within thirty (30) days of receipt by the DesignCommittee of all of the required materials, the proposed improvement or modification is deemed approved.
source_label: Rinn Valley Ranch Design Guidelines, Revision 7.2 (updated 12/10/2024), Sec. 4.1.1 and 4.1.2
notes: No fee amount is stated in the guidelines; Declaration Sec. 6.4 lets the committee set a reasonable fee, uniform or based on the improvement's estimated cost.

fact: Rinn Valley Ranch's Declaration deems a request approved unless the committee sends a disapproval or asks for more information within 30 days of receiving everything it needs.
quote: Any request for approval of a proposed Improvement or modification shall be deemed approved, unless disapproval or a request for additional information or materials is transmitted to the Applicant by the Committee within thirty days after the date of receipt by the Committee of all necessary materials as determined by the Committee.
source_label: Declaration of Covenants, Conditions and Restrictions of Rinn Valley Ranch, Sec. 6.8

fact: Rinn Valley Ranch's Declaration lets the committee ask for surveys, plot plans, drainage plans, elevations, specifications and material and color samples showing an improvement's shape, height, materials and location.
quote: Prior to commencement of work to accomplish any proposed Improvement, or any modification to any Improvement, the Person (“Applicant”) proposing to make the Improvement or modification shall submit to the Committee, at its offices, such descriptions, surveys, plot plans, drainage plans, elevation drawings, construction plans, specifications, and samples of materials and colors as the Committee shall reasonably request, showing the nature, kind, shape, height, width, color, materials, location of the proposed Improvement or modification thereof.
source_label: Declaration of Covenants, Conditions and Restrictions of Rinn Valley Ranch, Sec. 6.4

fact: Rinn Valley Ranch takes design requests through PayHOA, says no work should start until both the committee and the Town of Frederick have approved it, and requires a changed plan to be resubmitted.
quote: All DRC Requests must be submitted through PayHOA … NO CONSTRUCTION SHOULD OCCUR UNTIL THE HOME OWNER RECEIVES APPROVAL FROM THE COMMITTEE AND ANY NECESSARY APPROVALS AND PERMITS FROM THE TOWN OF FREDERICK. IF YOUR PLANS CHANGE AFTER APROVAL FROM THE DRC YOU MUST RESUMIT FOR ADDITIONAL APPROVAL.
source_label: Rinn Valley Ranch HOA, DRC - Design Review Committee page

fact: Rinn Valley Ranch's committee wants complete landscaping plans within 3 months of occupancy, with every plant named and shown at 5 years' growth, half the landscaping done within 12 months and the rest within 24.
quote: The Design Committee requires complete landscaping and specifications plans within three (3) months of occupancy. Existing and proposed landscaping material and all plants should be called out by name and show 5 year growth. No landscaping shall commence until plans are approved by the Design Committee. Once the landscaping plan is approved, half of the landscaping must be completed within 12 months of occupancy and the other half completed within 24 months of occupancy of the Dwelling.
source_label: Rinn Valley Ranch HOA, DRC - Design Review Committee page

fact: At the August 19, 2025 board meeting, Rinn Valley Ranch's committee reported a typical 3-business-day turnaround on requests, landscaping among them, and the minutes call projects built without approval covenant violations.
quote: Requests included landscaping, paint, chicken coop, sunroom and porch. … Typical 3 business day turnaround for requests. … Enforcement of DRC guidelines and homeowners that do not follow the DRC process. Projects without approval are community covenant violations. … The DRC committee will deny requests if the Project does not meet the guidelines. If the DRC committee cannot agree, the request will be escalated to the board.
source_label: Rinn Valley Ranch HOA Meeting Minutes, Tuesday, August 19, 2025 (DRC Committee report)

fact: Rinn Valley Ranch's schedule of fines charges $25 a month for a violation other than a vehicle infraction, starting 30 days after the first notice.
quote: For all infractions, the fee will be $25 per month, beginning 30 days after the initial notification, with the exception of vehicle infractions.
source_label: Rinn Valley Ranch HOA, Schedule of Fines and Fees (linked from the HOA Documents page)

fact: Rinn Valley Ranch's guidelines want an improvement finished within 8 months of starting work, with written notice of completion to the committee, which may inspect within 30 days.
quote: The Improvements shall be completed within eight (8) months after the foundation is dug or other material work is begun. … Upon completion the Owner shall give written notice of completion to the Design Committee. … Within such reasonable time as the Design Committee may determine, but in no case exceeding thirty (30) days from the receipt of such written notice of completion from the Owner or its duly authorized representative, the Design Committee may inspect the Improvements.
source_label: Rinn Valley Ranch Design Guidelines, Revision 7.2 (updated 12/10/2024), Sec. 4.3 Completed Work

fact: Rinn Valley Ranch's guidelines place landscaping so the existing topography is disturbed as little as possible, slope drainage away from structures at least 1 foot in 10, and make each lot carry uphill lots' runoff to the street gutter or the rear of the lot.
quote: All structures and landscaping elements shall be placed on the Lot so that the existing topography will be disturbed as little as possible. Drainage shall be away from structures at a minimum slope of one (1) foot in ten (10) feet. … Each site is responsible for accepting all drainage from uphill lots and diverting it away from critical areas on site (away from house foundations, driveways and garden or walk-out level features). Each lot is also responsible for diverting runoff water to the front street gutters or to the rear area of the lot.
source_label: Rinn Valley Ranch Design Guidelines, Revision 7.2 (updated 12/10/2024), Sec. 3.14 Site Drainage and Grading

fact: Rinn Valley Ranch's Declaration bars interfering with the drainage pattern the developer established unless the Design Review Committee approves it in writing.
quote: There shall be no interference with the established drainage pattern initially established by the Declarant over any portion of The Planned Community, except as approved in writing by the Design Review Committee.
source_label: Declaration of Covenants, Conditions and Restrictions of Rinn Valley Ranch, Sec. 11.3 Maintenance of Drainage Pattern

fact: Rinn Valley Ranch's Declaration warns that parts of the community may have potentially expansive soils and requires a soils report and an engineered foundation for every home.
quote: Because certain areas of The Planned Community may consist of potentially expansive soils, each Owner must provide the Committee with a satisfactory soils report and engineered foundation plan signed and stamped by a registered professional engineer licensed in the State of Colorado. All foundations must be engineered foundations.
source_label: Declaration of Covenants, Conditions and Restrictions of Rinn Valley Ranch, Sec. 7.22 Foundation Restrictions

fact: Rinn Valley Ranch allows at- or below-grade patios anywhere on a lot once landscape requirements are met, and caps retaining walls at 4 feet of brick, stone, stucco or treated wood, with a neighbor's approval for one within 2 feet of a shared lot line.
quote: Patios constructed of brick, stone, concrete, or other materials will be permitted anywhere on a lot as long as they are at or below grade level and all landscape requirements are met. … Walls used for retaining changes in grade must be constructed of brick, stone, stucco, or treated wood, and may not be more than four (4) feet in height. Any such walls built within two (2) feet of a common property line must meet approval of the adjacent property owners.
source_label: Rinn Valley Ranch Design Guidelines, Revision 7.2 (updated 12/10/2024), Sec. 3.12 Decks, Balconies, Patios, and Walls

fact: Rinn Valley Ranch's guidelines favor landscape plans that blend one yard into the next with similar plants and random clumps of trees along lot lines, discourage rigid property boundaries, and encourage exterior courtyards and semi-enclosed patios.
quote: The Intent of the approval process for landscaping is to encourage an open, flowing relationship between Lots. Any plan which defines a rigid property boundary is discouraged, while plans that blend one landscaped yard into another, through the use of similar planting materials and random clumps of trees along property lines, are encouraged. … There is no mandatory “style” of architecture in the Community. … plans which produce exterior courtyards and semi-enclosed patios, will be encouraged.
source_label: Rinn Valley Ranch Design Guidelines, Revision 7.2 (updated 12/10/2024), Sec. 3.19.1 and Sec. 3.20 Style and Quality

fact: Rinn Valley Ranch allows no exterior lighting beyond approved porch lights without the committee's written approval, which may permit subdued lighting whose source can't be seen from nearby homes.
quote: No exterior lighting, other than approved porch lights, shall be permitted on any lot except with the written approval of the Design Committee. Exterior lighting that is subdued and whose light source is not visible from surrounding dwellings may be permitted by the Design Committee for such purposes as illuminating entrances, decks, driveways, parking areas and other approved purposes.
source_label: Rinn Valley Ranch Design Guidelines, Revision 7.2 (updated 12/10/2024), Sec. 3.18 Exterior Lighting

fact: Rinn Valley Ranch sends any fence change to the committee, allows an open three-rail white PVC fence 52 inches high outside front and street-side yards, caps solid PVC at 6 feet and 60 linear feet per lot, and bans wire and chain link.
quote: Any fencing change requires DRC review. … An open three-rail white PVC fence, as depicted on Exhibit A, may be built anywhere on any lot except in the front yard and in any side yard abutting a street. Fence height shall be set at 52 inches from finished grade. … Solid PVC fencing shall not exceed six feet in height and shall conform to the solid fencing depicted on Exhibit B. … Solid fencing shall not exceed 60 linear feet on any lot. … Wire or chain link fencing is strictly prohibited.
source_label: Rinn Valley Ranch Design Guidelines, Revision 7.2 (updated 12/10/2024), Sec. 3.13 Fencing
notes: Nets are not mentioned. Sec. 3.13.5 allows welded wire fabric on the inside of the rail fence to contain pets; Sec. 3.13.6 allows decorative fencing up to 24 inches or 50% solid with approval.

fact: Rinn Valley Ranch sends every accessory structure to the committee, requires one of 200 square feet or more to match the house's finish, colors, features and windows, and bans metal storage sheds.
quote: Accessory structures 200 sq ft or less require DRC review. … Accessory structures 200 sq ft or more require DRC review and shall utilize the same finish material, colors, architectural features and windows which match the main structure. … Lanais, trellises, hot tubs, gazebos, solar collectors, greenhouses, shed, and other major structural improvements shall be complimentary with materials used in the construction of the home. … No metal storage sheds will be allowed.
source_label: Rinn Valley Ranch Design Guidelines, Revision 7.2 (updated 12/10/2024), Sec. 3.17 Accessory Structures

fact: The setback sheet on Rinn Valley Ranch's committee page says the neighborhood is zoned R-1 and keeps a detached accessory structure 55 feet from the front, 15 feet from the side and 5 feet from the rear lot lines.
quote: Applicable setbacks for Rinn Valley Ranch, which is zoned R-1. … Front Setbacks: … Detached accessory structure: 55 feet … Side Setbacks: … Detached accessory structure: 15 feet … Rear Setbacks: … Detached accessory structure: 5 feet
source_label: "Town of Frederick Setback Requirements" sheet for Rinn Valley Ranch (R-1), linked from the HOA's DRC page
notes: The HOA's April 8, 2026 minutes say setback rules changed and were posted on the website, and that the DRC does not control setbacks; the Town does. Corner lots take the front setback on both street sides.

fact: Rinn Valley Ranch's covenants cover 148 lots: 70 in Filing No. 1 and 78 annexed as Filing No. 2 in 2003.
quote: This Declaration and Plat established 70 Lots on the real property known as Rinn Valley Ranch Filing No. 1 … Seventy Eight (78) Lots are hereby created on this real property and are added to the Planned Community. … As a result of this annexation, the total number of Lots in the Planned Community is One Hundred Forty Eight (148).
source_label: First Amendment to the Declaration of Covenants, Conditions and Restrictions of Rinn Valley Ranch (acknowledged July 14, 2003)

fact: The statewide parcel file lists 148 residential parcels in Rinn Valley Ranch's two filings, with a median of about 0.55 acre, the middle half between 0.50 and 0.66 acre, and the largest about 1.1 acres.
quote: Query of Colorado Public Parcels, countyName 'Weld', subName LIKE '%RINN VALLEY%' (RINN VALLEY RANCH 1ST FG; RINN VALLEY RANCH 2ND FG FINAL PLAT): 161 parcels, 148 with landUseDsc "Residential"; residential landAcres median 0.5517, quartiles 0.5003 and 0.6645, minimum 0.4994, maximum 1.1000.
source_label: Colorado Public Parcels (statewide parcel file), Weld County, Rinn Valley Ranch 1st and 2nd filings, queried 2026-09-26

fact: Rinn Valley Ranch's HOA must maintain and repair the irrigation ditches shown on its plat, among them the Rink Lateral, the Rural Ditch and the Godding Ditch Lateral.
quote: As part of the foregoing described obligation, the Association shall manage, operate, care for, insure, maintain, repair and reconstruct the Rink Lateral, the Rural Ditch, … and the Godding Ditch Lateral identified on the Plat.
source_label: Declaration of Covenants, Conditions and Restrictions of Rinn Valley Ranch, Sec. 3.4
notes: The elided name is a third ditch company's ditch (Sec. 3.4 names four); it is left out of public text because it names a town outside NoCo's territory. The board's February 12, 2025 minutes say the HOA was still looking into who owns the ditches and who must maintain them (record frederick-co--rinn-valley-ranch.minutes-2025-02-ditches).

fact: Rinn Valley Ranch's Declaration says water in or flowing through the community's ditch laterals is not owned by the HOA and gives no owner any right to it.
quote: Any water located in or flowing through any ditch lateral located within the Planned Community is not owned by the Association and neither the Association nor any Owner shall have any rights or interest therein by virtue of this Declaration.
source_label: Declaration of Covenants, Conditions and Restrictions of Rinn Valley Ranch, Sec. 14.11 Lateral Water

fact: OpenStreetMap maps the Rinn Valley Ranch neighbourhood in Frederick west of I-25, with the West I-25 Frontage Road east of it at the same latitude.
quote: Rinn Valley Ranch | lat 40.1350100, lon -104.9938063 | Rinn Valley Ranch, Frederick, Weld County, Colorado, 80504, United States; West I-25 Frontage Road | lat 40.1351172, lon -104.9809642 | West I-25 Frontage Road, Weld County, Colorado, 80530, United States
source_label: OpenStreetMap Nominatim lookup: node 6245994985 (Rinn Valley Ranch) and way 1553247670 (West I-25 Frontage Road)
notes: Colorado DOLA municipal boundaries (data.colorado.gov w6jq-7em5) put points at 40.1387/-104.9950, 40.1360/-104.9900 and 40.1320/-104.9960 inside Frederick. The Town's water page says Frederick residents west of I-25 are Left Hand Water District customers (shared record frederick-two-providers).

fact: Rinn Valley Ranch's construction rules keep contractors' vehicles out of the ditches and off neighboring lots, park them on one side of the street, send excess excavation off site or where the committee says, and bar contractors from bringing dogs.
quote: Contractors, subcontractors, and material suppliers shall not drive through ditches or onto adjacent sites as they have been seeded or sodded. Contractor, subcontractor and material supply vehicles shall be parked on one side of the street only, as parking on both sides inhibits passage of other residents and emergency vehicles. … Excess excavation materials shall be hauled off the project or placed in areas designated by the Design Committee. … Trash and debris shall be removed from each Construction site at least once a week by every Friday to a dumping site located off the project. … The following practices are prohibited in the community. … E. Contractors bringing any animals or pets, particularly dogs, into the Community.
source_label: Rinn Valley Ranch Design Guidelines, Revision 7.2 (updated 12/10/2024), Sec. 5.3, 5.5, 5.8 and 5.10(E)

fact: Rinn Valley Ranch's HOA minutes remind owners that motorized vehicles may not travel along the ditch behind the homes on Cottonwood Circle and Homestead, and that materials left on the road overnight must be clearly marked.
quote: Motorized vehicles are not allowed to travel along the ditch behind the homes along Cottonwood Circle and Homestead. … If landscaping or other materials must be left on the road overnight, please clearly mark the piles.
source_label: Rinn Valley Ranch HOA Meeting Minutes, December 6, 2023 (community reminders; the same reminder appears in minutes from 2021 through 2023)

fact: Rinn Valley Ranch's own guidelines tell owners to follow the Town of Frederick's code and get every required permit before any landscaping work starts, and make all ground cover meet the Town's rules on height, location and maintenance.
quote: Before any work is started on the landscaping, the homeowner must follow Town of Frederick Municipal Code (http://www.codepublishing.com/co/frederick/) and obtain any and all required permits. … All ground cover and landscaping shall comply with all regulations and ordinances of the Town of Frederick with respect to height, location, and maintenance.
source_label: Rinn Valley Ranch Design Guidelines, Revision 7.2 (updated 12/10/2024), Sec. 3.19.5 and 3.19.6
notes: The codepublishing.com link in the guidelines predates Frederick's 2026 Land Use Code (effective June 1, 2026); the Town's turf rules are in shared records frederick-luc-16-4-80-artificial-turf and frederick-co.luc-2026-functional-artificial-turf-defined.

fact: At Rinn Valley Ranch's April 8, 2026 board meeting, the enforcement report said dry or brown lawns would not be subject to enforcement for 2026 while watering restrictions are in place, and the DRC report said setback rules had changed, were posted on the website, and are not the DRC's to control.
quote: With the watering restrictions in place, dry/brown lawns will not be subject to enforcement for 2026. … Several requests for outbuildings. The rules for setbacks have changed and posted on the website to help homeowners when planning a structure. However, DRC does not have control over setbacks.
source_label: Rinn Valley Ranch HOA Meeting Minutes, Wednesday, April 8, 2026 (Enforcement Committee and DRC reports)
notes: Linked from https://www.rinnvalleyranch.org/hoa-meeting-minutes (4/08/26), the latest minutes posted as of 2026-09-26. The same minutes say the Town emailed that watering would be limited for conservation and the HOA was looking at xeriscape for its west entrance.

fact: Rinn Valley Ranch's February 12, 2025 minutes say the HOA was still looking into who owns the community's ditches and who is responsible for maintaining them.
quote: HOA is still looking into the ownership of the ditches and the responsibilities of maintaining them.
source_label: Rinn Valley Ranch HOA Meeting Minutes, February 12, 2025 (Community Improvement report)
notes: Linked from https://www.rinnvalleyranch.org/hoa-meeting-minutes (2/12/25). Declaration Sec. 3.4 names the ditches the Association must maintain; later minutes posted through April 8, 2026 do not report an answer.
